prompt: Challenge C061-CH1: Our cold-pressed pumpkin seed oil goes rancid within 4 months on shelf, but competitors manage 9–12 months; we lose about 15% of each batch

content.text: {"expertise":[{"text":"Research on cold-pressed seed oils demonstrates that nitrogen flushing significantly reduces peroxide values compared to air headspace, with headspace oxygen residual levels above 2% accelerating oxidation, particularly under light exposure.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-02921","field":"abstract","quote":"Nitrogen flushing significantly reduced PV at day 30 and suppressed chlorophyll-mediated photosensitised oxidation"}]},{"text":"Work on lipid oxidation markers in cold-pressed oils shows that peroxide value alone can misrepresent oxidation stage, as fresh oil may display high peroxide values while secondary markers like p-anisidine value remain low, requiring multiple markers for accurate shelf-life prediction.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-02926","field":"abstract","quote":"high PV with low p-AV in freshly pressed oil versus low PV with elevated p-AV in oil approaching the end of its oxidative induction period"}]},{"text":"Research indicates that activated bleaching earth treatment removes chlorophyll and polar hydroperoxides from cold-pressed oils but causes simultaneous loss of tocopherol antioxidants, presenting a trade-off for operators seeking quality improvement without full refining.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-02924","field":"abstract","quote":"ABE treatment at 2% reduced initial PV by 38–55% across oil types but simultaneously caused a 12–29% loss of total tocopherols"}]}],"fit":"strong","fitReason":"The researcher's doctoral thesis specifically addressed peroxide formation kinetics in pumpkin seed oils [R0231], and published work directly investigates headspace oxygen effects on oxidation in cold-pressed oils [SYN-PUB-02921], oxidation marker interpretation [SYN-PUB-02926], and practical refining interventions [SYN-PUB-02924], all directly applicable to identifying oxidation pathways and implementable process changes without major equipment investment."}
